The question asks whether an infinite quadratically closed extension of the field with two elements exists. The algebraic closure of F_2 is algebraically closed, hence quadratically closed, and it is infinite. So the answer is Yes.

The submitted answer "yes" matches. Solve path 1 contains some muddled reasoning. For example, the union of F_{2^{2^k}} is not quadratically closed, since it has F_{2^3}-type extensions missing and its Galois group still has Z_2 factors. Actually, the Galois group of the union of F_{2^{2^k}} is the quotient of Ẑ for the supernatural number 2^∞, which is ∏_{p≠2} Z_p, so no index-2 subgroup exists and it is quadratically closed. That claim is fine. The final answer is Yes either way.
